references.text: The people feared the fire and thunder on Mount Sinai, which led Moses to become a mediator between God and the people.
The people asked Moses to speak to them instead of God, because they feared they would die if God spoke directly to them.
The people asked Moses to be a mediator because they feared the fire and the voice of God.
Moses reminds the people that they asked for a mediator at Horeb because they feared the fire.
Only Moses was to come near the Lord, while the people were not to approach.
Paul explains that the law was given through a mediator, pointing back to Moses' role between God and the people.
Jesus is the mediator of a better covenant, just as Moses was the mediator of the old covenant.
The author describes how the revelation at Sinai was so terrifying that the people could not endure what they heard and saw.
